definition: The setting world for grim and perilous adventures in the Fourth Edition core-product description.
cultural_caution: A fictional WFRP setting term, not a real historical period, character endpoint, or a claim that it is identical to every other Warhammer Old World product.

supports: Old World as the selected Fourth Edition game-setting context.

original_language: English WFRP Fourth Edition rules terminology
definition: The core rulebook’s category for four playable species: Human, Dwarf, Elf, and Halfling.
cultural_caution: A fictional tabletop character-option category, not a real-world racial category, character endpoint, or a statement about species in other editions or Warhammer games.

citations.locator: Official product page, feature list, ‘Four distinct Character Species’
supports: Character Species category and the four listed playable species.

original_language: English WFRP Fourth Edition rules terminology
definition: The core rulebook’s 64-option category representing what a character does when not adventuring.
cultural_caution: A game-mechanical vocation category, not a fixed biography, social judgment, or a character endpoint.

citations.locator: Official product page, feature list, ‘64 distinct careers’
supports: Careers as a selected Fourth Edition character-life-path category.

original_language: English WFRP Fourth Edition rules terminology
definition: The supernatural acts associated by the core-product description with priests of the Old World’s major religions.
cultural_caution: A fictional WFRP rules/setting term, not a real religious claim, a deity character endpoint, or an exhaustive theology.

citations.locator: Official product page, feature list, major religions and miracles
supports: Miracles as a selected religious-power category.

original_language: English WFRP Fourth Edition rules terminology
definition: The eight-category magic structure named in the core-product feature list.
cultural_caution: A source-specific magical-rules category, not a real spiritual tradition, a character, or an assertion that all Warhammer magic systems use this structure.

citations.locator: Official product page, feature list, ‘Spells from eight different magical traditions’
supports: Magical traditions as a selected Fourth Edition magic category.

definition: The fictional destructive influence described in the core-product setting text as tainting and altering people in the Old World.
cultural_caution: Fictional horror/setting language involving bodily alteration, disease, violence, and cult activity; it is not a medical, disability, religious, or moral category for real people.

citations.locator: Official product page, Old World description, Chaos paragraphs
supports: Chaos as a corrupting fictional force and its stated transformation/taint context.

definition: The game-system label supplied for the Fourth Edition Core Rulebook product.
cultural_caution: A rules-engine label, not a setting entity, an edition-equivalence claim, or a character endpoint.

citations.locator: Official physical-product page, additional information, ‘Game System: D100’
supports: D100 as the selected Core Rulebook game-system label.
